channel.title: Rest of Europe 1919-45
channel.description: Last 10 notes on Rest of Europe 1919-45

item.title: The Abwehr
item.description: The Abwehr The Abwehr was the German military intelligence service, the secret service of the Reichswehr and later of the Wehrmacht, and the great espionage apparatus of the Second World War.

item.title: Agrarian question in Spain
item.description: Agrarian question in Spain The agrarian question in Spain was the problem of the land — the maldistribution of the soil between a few great proprietors and the mass of the landless, and the poverty that flowed from it — which the Republic of 1931 inherited as the most ambitious problem facing the ne...

item.title: The Bloc National
item.description: The Bloc National The parliamentary majority and coalition that governed France in the five years after the Great War, from the legislative elections of 16 November 1919 to the triumph of the opposing Cartel des Gauches in May 1924.

item.title: Catalan question
item.description: Catalan question The Catalan question was the problem of the place of Catalonia within Spain — the demand of a distinct people, with its own language and its own economic life, for the recognition of its national personality and the government of its own affairs.

item.title: The Corporate State
item.description: The Corporate State The corporate state (stato corporativo) is the organisation of the Italian Fascist state by which the economy and the professions were regrouped, not as free associations of capital and labour in conflict, but as organs of the nation itself.

item.title: The Cult of the Personality
item.description: The Cult of the Personality The cult of the personality (культ личности, kul’t lichnosti) is the devotion paid to the leader in the Soviet order of the Stalin era — the public veneration of Iosif Vissarionovich Stalin as the disciple and successor of Lenin, the architect of socialism, and the Suprem...

item.title: Era of Tyrannies
item.description: Era of Tyrannies The era of tyrannies (l’ère des tyrannies) is the name the French historian and liberal philosopher Élie Halévy gave to the age that, in his reading, opened in August 1914 and came to dominate the interwar decades — the age of Italian Fascism, German National Socialism and Russian B...

item.title: Espionage in the Second World War
item.description: Espionage in the Second World War Espionage — the secret gathering of an enemy’s military and political knowledge by concealed agents, the secret war fought alongside the visible one — was raised by the Second World War to an instrument of mass organization.

item.title: L'Étrange Défaite
item.description: L’Étrange Défaite The “strange defeat” — the phrase and the diagnosis of Marc Bloch, the medieval historian and co-founder of the Annales school, for the collapse of France in May and June 1940.

item.title: Falange Española
item.description: Falange Española The Falange Española (Spanish Phalanx) is the name of the fascist movement that José Antonio Primo de Rivera founded in Spain in the autumn of 1933, and the formation to which the regime that triumphed in the Civil War was to attach its single-party line.
